result: **Recommendation: change the design.** Don't make the five statuses one mutually exclusive value. Your hypothesis holds up against the code. The only real either/or is the reason autosave has stopped: a **failure**, fixed by retrying, or a **conflict**, fixed by choosing a version. "Dirty" means the folder still owes storage a write. "Saving" means a write is in flight. Those two often overlap. Merging them into one status already loses information in this snapshot. The editor I'd build is `text` (always present), `pending`, `writing`, and `problem: SaveFailure | SaveConflict | undefined`. You get one with `await folder.open(path)`. Loading, missing-file and not-text outcomes come back from `open` instead of living on the editor as states. ## What I read ``` .agents/skills/adversarial-review/{SKILL.md, references/deletion-prizes.md} REQUEST.md packages/folder/src/{edit-owner.ts, edits.ts} packages/svelte/src/edits.ts packages/react/src/edits.ts apps/epicenter/src/folders/FileEditor.svelte apps/honeycrisp/src/routes/components/{NoteDetail,FileDetail(60–127)}.svelte apps/capture/src/lib/components/TextDetail.svelte apps/whispering/src/routes/components/RecordingDetail.svelte apps/whispering/src/lib/whispering.svelte.ts (485–534, 1035–1080) ``` I couldn't use `read_thread`, so this describes only what's in the snapshot. The nested proposal is implemented, but as `getBuffer()` → `BufferSnapshot` (`edit-owner.ts:141`) rather than a `fileEdit.buffer` property. The Svelte adapter exposes that as `.buffer`. ## Why one status misleads Here is what the code does today: - **`saving` can hide newer text.** Typing during a save keeps `saving: true` on the newer input (`edit-owner.ts:1152`). The status claims the current text is being saved when an older revision is. - **`saving` hides a failure during retry.** `drain` clears the error when an attempt starts (`:847`), so the "Try again" banner disappears and reappears. - **`saving` hides a conflict.** `submitText` schedules autosave unconditionally (`:1162`), even when a conflict is held. The attempt sends the stale `input.from` (`:827`), so it conflicts again unless storage happens to have changed back. On each pause in typing, status goes conflict → saving → conflict. The conflict panels in FileEditor, Capture and Honeycrisp, which check `status === 'conflict'`, flicker with it. - **No caller distinguishes dirty from saving.** FileEditor:81 and TextDetail:157–161 both show "Saving…" for either. Whispering's `isSaving` means "unsaved and not failed" (`whispering.svelte.ts:1039`). - **The display-priority compression is in `buffer.error`.** `refusal ?? read error ?? source issue` (`:573`) merges refusals, read failures and deletion into one field. Invalidating it takes about 60 lines (`:504–563`), even though every command already returns its refusal as a `Result`. ## Definitions - **Revision:** a counter that goes up each time a change to the text is accepted. - **Witness:** the exact stored bytes the current text was derived from, last read or last confirmed written by us. - **Saved(r):** storage confirmed it holds revision r's text, written while it still held the witness. The witness then becomes that text. - **Pending (dirty):** the folder owes storage a write. This is true while `input` exists. Text that equals the witness is still pending if a write of a different revision is in flight. - **`save()`:** resolves `Ok({ revision })` once some revision at least as new as the one at call time is confirmed. Otherwise it returns that attempt's error. Today it returns the whole drain loop's final outcome (`:806–808`, `:888`), so it can wait for later typing or report a later revision's failure. - **Flush:** remove it from the editor's vocabulary. It's internal in the owner. The public folder-level operation is `settle()`/`close()`: attempt every pending editor once and return what is still held. - **Memory vs durability:** pending text is memory. Crash recovery is a separate journal, and nothing in memory gets called "saved". ## Sequences 1. **Typing during a save.** r1 is being written; you type r2. Then `writing=true`, `pending=true`, `text=r2`. When r1 lands, the witness becomes r1, `writing=false`, r2 stays pending and autosave follows. A `save()` called at r1 resolves with `{revision: r1}` and doesn't wait for r2. 2. **Revert while a save runs.** The witness is w0 and r1 is in flight. `revert()` accepts r2 = w0's text. It stays pending because r1 will land and make storage differ from w0. After r1 lands, autosave writes w0's text back. The code already does this (`:1139–1147`). By contrast, `discard()` refuses with BUSY (`:1013`). Make `revert()` the one verb that never refuses. 3. **Retrying a failure.** `problem` = failure for r1. `save()` sets `writing=true` and keeps the failure until the attempt settles: success clears it, another failure replaces it. Typing r2 clears it, because it described r1, and schedules autosave. That last part is already implemented (`:1153`). 4. **Typing after a conflict.** A conflict describes the witness, not a revision, so every later revision inherits it. The conflict stays, typing is accepted, autosave is suspended, and `save()` returns the conflict without writing. Only `resolve('mine' | 'stored' | {text})` changes the witness. 5. **Refresh fails, text still usable.** The editor state doesn't change. `refresh()` returns the error to its caller, and the polling query (`createQuery(queries.read(...))`) already owns that error. 6. **Refresh finds the file deleted.** - **With pending text:** `problem = Conflict{stored: null}` and the text stays. `resolve('mine')` recreates the file. `resolve('stored')` releases the editor. - **Clean:** today the text disappears (`shownText` → undefined, status `unavailable`). FileEditor works around this with `lastShown` and a readonly box (`FileEditor.svelte:54–64`). Under the "text always exists" promise, a clean editor shows the same deletion conflict with `pending=false`. Typing is held but not written. - **Cost:** this is the one case where a clean editor doesn't follow storage. Clean editors still adopt outside *modifications* automatically. ## Proposed API ```ts folder.open(path): Promise> folder.peek(path): Result | undefined // already held: no loading flash type Editor = { readonly path: string; readonly text: string; // always readonly pending: boolean; // folder owes storage a write readonly writing: boolean; // an attempt is in flight, possibly of an older revision readonly problem: SaveFailure | SaveConflict | undefined; // exclusive: retry vs choose markdown(schema: S): MarkdownContent; replaceText(text: string): Result; change(doc: DocumentChange): Result; revert(): void; // text := witness text save(): Promise>; resolve(choice: 'mine' | 'stored' | { text: string }): Promise>; refresh(): Promise>; subscribe(fn: () => void): () => void; }; ``` Invariants: a failure implies `pending`, and so does `writing`. A conflict means writes are suspended. Failure and conflict never coexist; a conflict replaces a failure. Vanilla use: ```ts const opened = await folder.open('notes/a.md'); if (opened.error) return show(opened.error); const editor = opened.data; editor.replaceText(editor.text + '\nMore.'); const saved = await editor.save(); if (saved.error?.name === 'Conflict') await editor.resolve('mine'); ``` Svelte: ```svelte {#await folder.peek(path) ?? folder.open(path)} {:then opened} {#if opened.error} {:else}{/if} {/await} {#if conflict}Not saved: the file changed elsewhere {:else if editor.problem}Not saved{editor.writing ? ' · retrying…' : ''} {:else if editor.pending}Saving… {:else}Saved{/if} {#if conflict} {:else if editor.problem} {/if}
